data.long_meaning: Derived from Old Norse 'hrolf' meaning 'infamous ruler' or 'wolf power'. The name Rollo is associated with the famous Viking ruler of Normandy in France. The name Rollo carries the meaning “Wolf power” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English. Parents who choose Rollo usually hope their child will grow to embody wolf power and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: Rollo is most notably known for his role in the history of spreading the influence of the Viking people and their culture beyond Scandinavia to the shores of France. As the Duke of Normandy, Rollo's military conquests expanded theNorman kingdom into Gaul and facilitated the establishment of the Norman Dynasty. Chronicling the political and territorial accomplishments of Rollo, his name remains synonymous with Nordic expansion and the spread of Viking influence beyond their homeland.
data.spiritual_significance: In the religious context, Rollo is most famously recorded for his conversion to Christianity in 913 AD. According to Encarta, after assuming the duchy of Normandy, Rollo “began to engage in various schemes to buttress his power.” In an attempt to form an alliance with Charles III, the King of West Francia, Rollo agreed to be baptized and submit to Frankish rule. The delicate political scene brought about the ultimate question for Rollo: would he be a pagan Viking or Christian Duke? He chose the latter, and his conversion had profound effects not only for him, but also for Normandy and the early Western European Christian church. The cooperation and peace between Rollo and Charles III set the precedent for future alliances and lasting influence between the Scandinavian and continental Christian powers. Thus, Rollo represents a pivotal time in history when pagan Norse and Christian European powers came together and set the stage for Christianization in the Nordic world.
